findings.title: up still runs a llama-swap behind or ahead of the pin that no pinned digest ever checked, the v270 the phase-2 finding named among them
findings.cause: the fix of the phase-2 review's finding 8 checks the `archive.sha256` record only when the current release is PINNED.release (`release != PINNED.release || digest == pinned`); any other release from v267 on passes target with no look at its record, and doctor's Behind and Ahead arms only warn. A v267 to v270, or a v272 and later, that ai-ctl 0.2.0's `gateway install --version <N>` installed against the checksums file published on the same release page (0.2.0's DigestSource::Published, "detects a corrupt download, not a replaced one"), or with a digest the user typed, has no record, and once `current` names it `up` starts it as the gateway, with the key and every prompt
findings.consequence: attacker: whoever writes a llama-swap release's archive and its checksums file (§1, last row), before the user ran 0.2.0's `--version` on it. The control docs/security.md states, the pinned SHA-256 as "the only source of trust" and llama-swap "updated only through ai-ctl's pin", is applied after the upgrade to v271 alone: a v270 carried over from 0.2.0 as `current` runs under `up` with no record, where an unrecorded v271 is refused, the exact case the finding this fixes named ("a v270 or v271"). The binary already ran once at its install (`-version`), as the user, so a refusal now takes back no code already run: the control is weakened, no damage shown. On this machine `current` names v271, and v270 sits beside it unrecorded
findings.fix: have target, and doctor's Behind and Ahead arms, accept a release other than the pin only when its directory holds a record (only an ai-ctl from 0.3.0 on writes one, and only after checking the archive against its own pin); without one, up refuses it with `ai-ctl gateway install` and doctor fails, as for the pinned release; say so in docs/security.md §7 and in `up`'s refusals in docs/commands.md
findings.test: up refuses a current v270 whose directory records no digest (FakeReleases::current("v270") with record None), where today it starts the gateway; doctor fails on the same
findings.evidence: reproduced: in a copy of `docs(review): complete the review of review-skill-v2-5 phase 2` of 2026-11-12, a test beside up_refuses_the_pinned_release_never_checked_against_its_pin with `FakeReleases::current(release)` and `record = None` for "v270" and "v272": `world.up()` returns Ok and `gateway.started` is 1 for each (cargo test --lib review_probe: ok); read: src/application/lifecycle.rs:781-785, the `release != PINNED.release ||` short-circuit; base src/application/gateway.rs at `chore(release): release 0.2.0` of 2026-11-06, DigestSource::Published and Given for any release but the pinned v263; `ls -la ~/.local/share/ai-ctl/llama-swap/v270/` holds `llama-swap` and no `archive.sha256`

findings.title: gateway install re-checks the pinned release under a running gateway, which then keeps the never-checked binary while status, up and doctor take it for the checked one
findings.cause: since this scope, publish removes an installed release's directory when it records no digest or another one and renames the re-checked one into the same path; a gateway started from the old `v271/llama-swap` keeps running its unlinked inode. liveness_of takes `<path> (deleted)` for the recorded binary, and is_current compares only the recorded path with target's, the same path, so the running gateway reads as Running on the current configuration; install neither takes the gateway's lock nor says a gateway runs the binary it replaced
findings.consequence: attacker: as in the finding above, whoever wrote a release archive an older ai-ctl installed without the pinned digest. The documented control, "`up` refuses to run it until then", holds for a new start only: after the remedy doctor gives, `ai-ctl gateway install`, the gateway that runs the never-checked binary keeps the key and the prompts until the user happens to run `down`, while `up` answers that the gateway runs, `status` shows the configuration current and doctor's llama-swap check passes. The binary had already run as the user, so no damage is shown beyond what the install allowed; the user is told the control is in force when the process it guards is not covered
findings.fix: Inspector::is_current counts a gateway whose /proc/<pid>/exe ends in ` (deleted)` as Outdated (the binary was replaced since it started), so status, doctor and up name `ai-ctl down && ai-ctl up`; and `gateway install`, when a recorded gateway runs from the release it replaces, warns that it runs the old binary until restarted
findings.test: with a gateway record whose process runs a binary since replaced (the probe below as a fixture), status reports the configuration Outdated and up refuses with `ai-ctl down`, then `ai-ctl up`, where today they report it current
findings.evidence: reproduced: in a copy of `docs(review): complete the review of review-skill-v2-5 phase 2` of 2026-11-12, a test that starts a copy of /usr/bin/sleep as `<root>/llama-swap/v271/llama-swap` with no record, then FsGatewayStore::stage, copies a binary in, and publish(&staged, &pinned): digest(v271) becomes the pinned one, /proc/<pid>/exe reads `<root>/llama-swap/v271/llama-swap (deleted)`, liveness_of(pid, store.binary(v271)) returns Liveness::Running, and store.binary(v271) equals the path the process started from (cargo test --lib review_probe: ok; child killed and reaped); read: src/application/lifecycle.rs:250-263, up returning Up::Running when is_current holds and the gateway answers

findings.title: test_guard.py's child() leaves its process's stdout open, a ResourceWarning in a green run
findings.cause: child() opens the listener with `stdout=subprocess.PIPE` and registers its kill and wait as cleanups, never the pipe's close, so unittest's cleanup prints `ResourceWarning: unclosed file <_io.TextIOWrapper name=3>`
findings.consequence: no effect on the guard; the check's output carries a warning every run, beside which a new one passes unread
findings.fix: `self.addCleanup(process.stdout.close)` after the kill and wait cleanups, as orphan() closes its shell's stdout
findings.test: none: the check's own output, the warning gone
findings.evidence: reproduced: `python3 .claude/skills/reviewing-delivered-code/evals/test_guard.py` at `docs(review): complete the review of review-skill-v2-5 phase 2` of 2026-11-12, 37 tests OK with `ResourceWarning: unclosed file <_io.TextIOWrapper name=3 encoding='UTF-8'>`
